record.title: A preprint reports smaller validation-loss gaps for two 4-bit AdamW state schemes, with reproduction still open
record.summary: An October 8 arXiv preprint introduces ZIP-SR, which chooses stochastic-rounding probabilities in AdamW preconditioner space, and ZE-EDEN, which calibrates a zero-excluding second-moment codebook. The authors report 1.0625 bytes per parameter for persistent optimizer moments versus 8 bytes for FP32 moments, and smaller mean validation-loss gaps to 32-bit AdamW than TorchAO 4-bit AdamW across evaluated GPT- and Llama-style pretraining runs from 130M to 2.7B parameters. At 1.4B parameters, the paper reports the largest gap reduction, 70.1%; at 2.7B the TorchAO run diverged late, so the paper does not give a percentage comparison there. In full-parameter SFT, the two methods report lower validation loss than TorchAO and results close to 32-bit on downstream tasks, without a consistent downstream advantage. These are author-reported preprint results, not independently reproduced.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv paper defines ZIP-SR, which retains zero in the second-moment codebook and selects stochastic-rounding probabilities in preconditioner space, and ZE-EDEN, which uses a zero-excluding codebook with EDEN block calibration. It links PyTorch implementations and example scripts.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across the paper’s GPT- and Llama-style pretraining experiments from 130M to 2.7B parameters, the authors report both methods reduce TorchAO 4-bit AdamW’s mean validation-loss gap to 32-bit AdamW at each evaluated size. The largest stated reduction is 70.1% at 1.4B; the 2.7B TorchAO run diverged late and is not assigned a percentage reduction.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For full-parameter supervised fine-tuning, the paper reports lower validation loss than TorchAO 4-bit AdamW and results close to 32-bit AdamW on downstream tasks, without a consistent downstream-task advantage.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper calculates persistent moment storage of 1.0625 bytes per parameter for its two 4-bit configurations, versus 8 bytes per parameter for two FP32 moment buffers; this is optimizer-state storage, not total training memory.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported validation-loss comparisons and storage behavior have not been independently reproduced.
Paper storage accounting covers persistent moments, but total peak memory and runtime impact are not established by the reported per-parameter storage ratio.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported validation-loss behavior holds across independent runs, reducing AdamW moment storage from 8 to 1.0625 bytes per parameter while retaining training quality could expand memory headroom for model size or batch capacity. The evidence is a single preprint with a small number of paired seeds and no independent reproduction; the result concerns optimizer-state storage, not total training memory or universal scaling.
limitations: Results come from one arXiv preprint and were not independently reproduced.
Pretraining comparisons use three paired seeds; supervised fine-tuning uses five. Uncertainty and robustness beyond these runs remain open.
At 2.7B the TorchAO reference diverged late; the paper reports no percentage gap reduction for that comparison.
The 1.0625-versus-8 bytes per parameter calculation covers persistent optimizer moment storage, not parameters, activations, temporary buffers, allocator overhead or total peak job memory.
Lower SFT validation loss does not yield a consistent downstream-task advantage in the reported results.
No evidence here establishes faster training, lower cost, broad model-family transfer or production adoption.
brief.summary: An October 8 arXiv preprint introduces ZIP-SR, which chooses stochastic-rounding probabilities in AdamW preconditioner space, and ZE-EDEN, which calibrates a zero-excluding second-moment codebook. The authors report 1.0625 bytes per parameter for persistent optimizer moments versus 8 bytes for FP32 moments, and smaller mean validation-loss gaps to 32-bit AdamW than TorchAO 4-bit AdamW across evaluated GPT- and Llama-style pretraining runs from 130M to 2.7B parameters. At 1.4B parameters, the paper reports the largest gap reduction, 70.1%; at 2.7B the TorchAO run diverged late, so the paper does not give a percentage comparison there. In full-parameter SFT, the two methods report lower validation loss than TorchAO and results close to 32-bit on downstream tasks, without a consistent downstream advantage. These are author-reported preprint results, not independently reproduced.

technical.claimed_result: The preprint reports that ZIP-SR and ZE-EDEN reduce TorchAO 4-bit AdamW’s mean validation-loss gap to 32-bit AdamW across tested pretraining sizes; the largest reported reduction is 70.1% at 1.4B. At 2.7B the TorchAO run diverges late, so no percentage is reported.
technical.demonstrated_result: The preprint specifies the methods, experimental regime and storage accounting and links implementation code. Training performance remains author-reported; no reproduction occurred in this review.
technical.mechanism: ZIP-SR keeps zero in the second-moment codebook but computes stochastic rounding probabilities in the space of induced AdamW preconditioners. ZE-EDEN instead excludes zero and rescales quantized second-moment blocks using EDEN calibration. Both pair this with NF4 first moments and targeted LM-head stochastic rounding in the final 10% of training.
technical.regime: GPT- and Llama-style pretraining at 130M–2.7B parameters; three paired seeds per pretraining comparison. Full-parameter SFT on Qwen3-8B and Llama3.2-3B uses five seeds. Paper reports H200 accelerators except GPT 2.7B on B200. Persistent moment storage comparison is 1.0625 versus 8 bytes per parameter.
technical.reproducibility: The paper links PyTorch implementations and scripts at https://github.com/nubank/adamw4bit. This review inspected the full HTML paper and did not execute the code or reproduce the experiments. Seed counts and accelerator types are reported in Appendix B.
technical.strongest_baseline: TorchAO 4-bit AdamW at the same persistent moment-storage bit budget; 32-bit AdamW is the reference for validation-loss gap.

brief.title: A preprint reports smaller validation-loss gaps for two 4-bit AdamW state schemes, with reproduction still open
brief.why_it_matters: Optimizer moments consume substantial persistent memory during training. If these methods reproduce under matched hardware and training budgets, they could free memory for other training needs at the same optimizer-state bit budget. The paper compares only its evaluated settings; it does not establish that total job memory falls by the same ratio, that training is faster, or that downstream quality improves consistently.
